title: macOS install is hard-broken: comfyui_controlnet_aux requires onnxruntime-gpu, which has no macOS wheels
description: Every macOS user fails first install on any depth model. The pinned comfyui_controlnet_aux requirements.txt ends with an unmarked onnxruntime-gpu; that package is CUDA-only and publishes no macOS wheel at any version, so pip cannot resolve it, the custom command exits 1, and the whole node install is marked failed. Retry re-runs the identical command, so it can never succeed. LOCAL engine only - the Pod bakes this node into a CUDA Linux image.
acceptance: A macOS install of any depth model completes without the Installation Failed dialog
onnxruntime-gpu is stripped from the node's requirements.txt on darwin before EITHER install path reads it (installRequirementsCommand and the default pip -r branch)
Windows and Linux are byte-unchanged - the file is only rewritten when a line is actually dropped, so no platform that can resolve the wheel loses it
Idempotent: a second run over an already-filtered file changes nothing and does not re-log
Filter is a pure exported helper with a unit test covering drop, no-op, and versioned-specifier lines
tests/controlnet-aux-torch-guard.test.cjs still passes - the torch guard on this dep must not regress
Remote/Pod path untouched and explicitly confirmed unaffected

attention.reason: Needs a real macOS install of a depth model. Code-verified and negative-controlled, but no Apple hardware was available. macOS validation is coordinated by the MPI-391 umbrella (1.3.0 cross-platform sweep) - section C.
